authoredFrom: Why a separate expectation: the runtime recording journey (ET-015a PR-4, scripts/ci/recording-observation.mjs) serves normal-delivery.json with its transport replaced by three durable connections and one step appended. Connection 1 (0 ms, ack dropAfter:4) commits events 1-5 and loses the ACK of 5 before its scripted disconnect at 350 ms; the telemetry service is then terminated and main's supervisor restarts it. Connection 2 (360 ms) is taken by the restarted service after the main window was closed to the tray; the application then exits from the tray. Connection 3 (2,010 ms) is taken by run B, the restarted application, and receives the appended simulation.paused at 2,100 ms.

Events: eventSeq 1-9 are normal-delivery's (normal-delivery.expected.json: truck, trailer, job, simulation.started, job re-send, simulation.paused, simulation.started, job.delivered, job.cleared at atMs 10, 20, 30, 40, 300, 400, 500, 600 and 610) and 10 is the appended simulation.paused at 2,100 ms; each UTC label is 1,800,000,000,000 + atMs. Each is stored once, and every first commit was a first delivery: the redelivered eventSeq 5 on connection 2 is a duplicate of its row from connection 1. No gap is stored.

Samples (ET-015b PR-3, H3-H9): connection 1's checkpoint is the plugin session's baseline, and its snapshot of the frame at 100 ms (simulation running since 40 ms) is the only fresh running reading of second 1000; it names trip@3, committed earlier in the FIFO. That row is stored only when the service's 5 s sample flush ran before the diagnostic kill (H9), so the journey accepts zero or one row and records the count. The checkpoints of connections 2 and 3 are the baselines of new recorders, and no frame follows them, so nothing else is sampled. PR-4 extends the journey with asserted sample rows.

Events 1-5 commit as in normal-delivery: the job (3) opens trip@3 partial with opened-at-load (T12), truck 1 and trailer 2 are its references, and the road stop 100 -> 200 persists observed distance 0 m at eventSeq 5 (T16).

docs/trips.md cold start (R4): the restarted service seeds the stored open trip of the same plugin session (job key of eventSeq 3, last label 1,800,000,000,300 of eventSeq 5, stored distance 0, not cleared), resumes it active and queues a consumer-restart not-connected interval; the trip is already partial, so no trip.update. The redelivered eventSeq 5 lies at the processed point, so the reducer skips it (T5).

The first new commit (eventSeq 6) carries the queued interval; the pause (6) and resume (7) add nothing else, as in normal-delivery. job.delivered (8) attributes to the trip and closes it {delivered, outcome, partial} at its label 1,800,000,000,600; the distance is unchanged (0 m), so no update. job.cleared (9) adds nothing.
Run B: the third service finds no stored open trip of ETS2 (R4), so it seeds nothing and records no interval; the appended simulation.paused (10) adds no trip effect. Coverage is 10.
